claim: An employer's failure to investigate internal complaints of ethnic harassment within a reasonable timeframe constitutes constructive notice of a hostile work environment. The Fifth Circuit held that managerial inaction lasting more than sixty days following a documented complaint is sufficient to establish employer liability under Title VII.
citation: Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp., 78 F.3d 541 (5th Cir. 1996)
initial_reasoning: The Fifth Circuit in Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp., 78 F.3d 541 (5th Cir. 1996) held that an employer’s failure to promptly investigate a documented complaint of racial/ethnic harassment can give rise to constructive notice, and it identified a delay of roughly sixty days after the complaint as unreasonable and sufficient to establish liability under Title VII. The citation directly supports the claim.

final_reasoning: In Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp., 78 F.3d 541 (5th Cir. 1996), the Fifth Circuit rejected the notion that a 60‑day delay in investigating a documented racial harassment complaint automatically created constructive notice of a hostile environment; the court required a more substantial showing of employer knowledge and tolerance. Thus the citation does not support the claim as stated.
